docs.title: 🛠️ Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git: Ensure that git is installed on your machine. Download Git
  • Python 3.12: Required for the project. Download Python
  • UV: Used for managing Python environments. Install UV

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

sh git clone https://github.com/CogitoNTNU/AvinorCompetition.git cd AvinorCompetition

  1. Install dependencies:

sh uv sync

  1. Set up pre commit (only for development): sh uv run pre-commit install

To build and preview the documentation site locally:

docs.title: Historisk ruteprogram
docs.text:
Datasett med flybevegelser, planlagte og faktiske avgangs- og landingstider, flyplasser, flyselskap, flyvningstype, mm. Datasettet utleveres som CSV.

Fil: historical_flights.csv

Vi har brukt datasettet over (historical_flights.csv) til å lage et enkelt datasett for trening. I vårt treningssett har vi laget et par enkle features til inspirasjon. docs.title: Samtidighet
docs.text:
Samtidighet skjer når flere fly (avganger eller ankomster) finner sted samtidig eller svært nært i tid på de flyplassene én AFIS-fullmektig overvåker.

Når en AFIS-fullmektig er i aktiv dialog med to eller flere fly samtidig, oppstår samtidighet.

docs.title: Kommunikasjonstider
docs.text:
• Landinger: AFIS-fullmektig kommuniserer med flyene fra 16 minutter før til 5 minutter etter landing
  • Avganger: AFIS-fullmektig kommuniserer med flyene fra 15 minutter før til 8 minutter etter avgang

docs.title: Lufttrafikktjenesten (LTT)
docs.text:
Lufttrafikktjenesten i Avinor refererer til tjenestene som sikrer sikker og effektiv flytrafikk i norsk luftrom. Dette inkluderer:

  • Flygeledere
  • AFIS (Aerodrome Flight Information Service)
  • LTT-fullmektiger som jobber med flysikring

docs.title: AFIS-fullmektig
docs.text: En AFIS-fullmektig (Aerodrome Flight Information Service Officer) er en person som gir flygeinformasjonstjeneste til luftfartøy på og rundt mindre flyplasser.

docs.title: Ansvar og oppgaver
docs.text:
• Gir piloter informasjon om vær, trafikk og forhold på flyplassen
  • Sørger for trygg og effektiv flyging
  • Viktig forskjell: I motsetning til større flyplasser, har AFIS-fullmektig ikke ansvaret for at det er trygge forhold for å lande - de gir kun piloten informasjon om forholdene på flyplassen

docs.title: Multippel drift
docs.text: Multippel drift betyr i denne sammenhengen at én AFIS-fullmektig betjener flere lufthavner samtidig (opptil tre lufthavner) fra én arbeidsstasjon i Remote Towers Centre (RTC).

docs.title: Teknologi
docs.text:
Dette er muliggjort ved hjelp av avansert teknologi som: - Kameraer - Mikrofoner - Annen sensorteknologi

Dette gir AFIS-fullmektigen full oversikt over situasjonen ved hver av de tilknyttede flyplassene.

docs.title: Mål med multippel drift
docs.text:
• 💰 Kostnadseffektivitet: Redusere kostnader og øke effektiviteten i lufttrafikktjenesten
  • 📈 Økt kapasitet: Øke kapasiteten til Avinor Flysikring ved bruk av ny teknologi
  • 🛡️ Flysikkerhet: Sikre høy flysikkerhet ved å optimalisere arbeidsbelastningen til AFIS-fullmektig, selv ved noe samtidighet av trafikk mellom flyplassene

docs.title: Steps to Update requirements.txt
docs.text:
By following these steps, you maintain an accurate and up-to-date requirements.txt file that reflects your project's dependencies. This practice enhances collaboration, simplifies the setup process for new developers, and ensures smooth deployment across different environments.

1. Create a Virtual Environment

Run the following command to create a virtual environment named venv:

 uv venv

2. Activate the Virtual Environment

Before installing or updating packages, activate the virtual environment.

On windows:

source .venv/Scripts/activate

On linux and mac:

source venv/bin/activate

3. Install Existing Dependencies

Install all the packages listed in the current requirements.txt file:

uv pip install -r requirements.txt

4. Install New Packages

If you've added new imports to your code that require additional packages, install them using pip.

For each new package, run:

uv pip install [package]

Replace package_name with the name of the package you need.

  1. Update the requirements.txt File

After installing the new packages, update the requirements.txt file to include all currently installed packages and their versions:

uv pip freeze > requirements.txt

This command overwrites the existing requirements.txt file with an updated list of all packages installed in the virtual environment.

6. Deactivate the Virtual Environment*

Once you've updated the requirements.txt file, deactivate the virtual environment:

deactivate

You can also opt to kill your terminal to deactivate the virtual enviroment.

docs.title: src.concurrency
docs.text:
Concurrency utilities: compute arrivals/departures per airport and coverage diagnostics.

Main functions: - compute_concurrency_with_coverage(...) -> (counts_time, counts_day, coverage_df) - save_concurrency_tables(...)

Design notes: - Uses scheduled times only: std for departures and sta for arrivals. - Builds hourly or daily counts and always includes a master airport list (from df_airports or inferred from flights) so outputs contain zeros instead of NaNs. - Returns a per-airport coverage summary so you can filter out airports with insufficient data.

Functions:

  • compute_concurrency_with_coverage –

    Compute concurrency (arrivals/departures) plus per-airport coverage.

  • create_concurrency_lookup_dataset –

    Create and save a concurrency lookup dataset for fast feature engineering.

  • load_concurrency_lookup –

    Load pre-computed concurrency lookup dataset.

docs.title: compute_concurrency_with_coverage
docs.text:
compute_concurrency_with_coverage(df_flights: DataFrame, df_airports: Optional[DataFrame] = None, freq: str = 'H', start: Optional[Timestamp] = None, end: Optional[Timestamp] = None, include_master_only: bool = True, min_hours_covered: int = 0, by_groups: bool = False) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]

Compute concurrency (arrivals/departures) plus per-airport coverage.

Returns (counts_time, counts_day, coverage_df).

Parameters - df_flights: flights with 'std' and 'sta' and airport columns (dep_airport/arr_airport or similar) - df_airports: optional master list with 'iata_code' column - freq: 'H' or 'D' for hourly/daily counts - start/end: optional datetimes to bound the time series - include_master_only: if True, the output airports set will be the master airport list; otherwise include any airport observed in the flights data as well. - min_hours_covered: post-filter threshold: airports with fewer than this many non-empty hour-buckets will be flagged in coverage but not automatically removed (you can use coverage_df to filter downstream) - by_groups: if True, aggregate by airport groups instead of individual airports

Source code in src/concurrency.py 
def compute_concurrency_with_coverage(
    df_flights: pd.DataFrame,
    df_airports: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    freq: str = "H",
    start: Optional[pd.Timestamp] = None,
    end: Optional[pd.Timestamp] = None,
    include_master_only: bool = True,
    min_hours_covered: int = 0,
    by_groups: bool = False,
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute concurrency (arrivals/departures) plus per-airport coverage.

    Returns (counts_time, counts_day, coverage_df).

    Parameters
    - df_flights: flights with 'std' and 'sta' and airport columns (dep_airport/arr_airport or similar)
    - df_airports: optional master list with 'iata_code' column
    - freq: 'H' or 'D' for hourly/daily counts
    - start/end: optional datetimes to bound the time series
    - include_master_only: if True, the output airports set will be the master airport list; otherwise
      include any airport observed in the flights data as well.
    - min_hours_covered: post-filter threshold: airports with fewer than this many non-empty hour-buckets
      will be flagged in coverage but not automatically removed (you can use coverage_df to filter downstream)
    - by_groups: if True, aggregate by airport groups instead of individual airports
    """
    assert freq in ("H", "D"), "freq must be 'H' or 'D'"

    # Normalize some common column names
    flights = df_flights.copy()
    # Common airport column alternatives
    dep_col = next(
        (
            c
            for c in ["dep_airport", "origin", "departure_airport", "dep"]
            if c in flights.columns
        ),
        "dep_airport",
    )
    arr_col = next(
        (
            c
            for c in ["arr_airport", "destination", "arrival_airport", "arr"]
            if c in flights.columns
        ),
        "arr_airport",
    )

    # Handle airport groups aggregation
    if by_groups:
        dep_group_col = next(
            (c for c in ["dep_airport_group", "origin_group"] if c in flights.columns),
            "dep_airport_group",
        )
        arr_group_col = next(
            (
                c
                for c in ["arr_airport_group", "destination_group"]
                if c in flights.columns
            ),
            "arr_airport_group",
        )

        # Use groups as the aggregation unit
        dep_col = dep_group_col
        arr_col = arr_group_col

        # Master list is unique groups
        dep_groups = (
            flights[dep_group_col].dropna().unique().tolist()
            if dep_group_col in flights.columns
            else []
        )
        arr_groups = (
            flights[arr_group_col].dropna().unique().tolist()
            if arr_group_col in flights.columns
            else []
        )
        master = sorted(set(dep_groups) | set(arr_groups))
    else:
        # Master airports list
        master = _infer_master_airports(flights, df_airports)

    # If include_master_only is False, extend master with any observed airports in flights
    if not include_master_only:
        observed = set()
        if dep_col in flights.columns:
            observed.update(flights[dep_col].dropna().unique().tolist())
        if arr_col in flights.columns:
            observed.update(flights[arr_col].dropna().unique().tolist())
        master = sorted(set(master) | observed)

    # Determine time bounds
    stds = pd.to_datetime(flights.get("std", pd.Series([])), errors="coerce")
    stas = pd.to_datetime(flights.get("sta", pd.Series([])), errors="coerce")
    min_time = min(
        (t for t in [stds.min(skipna=True), stas.min(skipna=True)] if pd.notna(t)),
        default=None,
    )
    max_time = max(
        (t for t in [stds.max(skipna=True), stas.max(skipna=True)] if pd.notna(t)),
        default=None,
    )

    if min_time is None or max_time is None:
        raise ValueError("No valid scheduled times (std/sta) found in flights")

    start_ts = (
        pd.to_datetime(start)
        if start is not None
        else pd.to_datetime(min_time).floor("D")
    )
    end_ts = (
        pd.to_datetime(end) if end is not None else pd.to_datetime(max_time).ceil("D")
    )

    # Convert freq for pandas compatibility ('H' -> 'h')
    pandas_freq = "h" if freq == "H" else freq
    time_index = pd.date_range(start=start_ts, end=end_ts, freq=pandas_freq)
    daily_index = pd.date_range(
        start=start_ts.floor("D"), end=end_ts.floor("D"), freq="D"
    )

    # Counts
    deps = _counts_by_time(flights, "std", dep_col, freq, time_index, master)
    arrs = _counts_by_time(flights, "sta", arr_col, freq, time_index, master)

    # Label columns
    deps.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([deps.columns.tolist(), ["departures"]])
    arrs.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([arrs.columns.tolist(), ["arrivals"]])

    counts_time = pd.concat([deps, arrs], axis=1).sort_index(axis=1)

    # Daily aggregates
    deps_daily = _counts_by_time(flights, "std", dep_col, "D", daily_index, master)
    arrs_daily = _counts_by_time(flights, "sta", arr_col, "D", daily_index, master)
    deps_daily.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
        [deps_daily.columns.tolist(), ["departures"]]
    )
    arrs_daily.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
        [arrs_daily.columns.tolist(), ["arrivals"]]
    )
    counts_day = pd.concat([deps_daily, arrs_daily], axis=1).sort_index(axis=1)

    # Coverage summary
    coverage = []
    total_buckets = len(time_index)
    entity_type = "group" if by_groups else "airport"
    for entity in master:
        # count non-zero hourly buckets where entity has any event
        if entity in counts_time.columns.get_level_values(0):
            # select both departures and arrivals for this entity
            try:
                dep_series = counts_time[(entity, "departures")]
            except KeyError:
                dep_series = pd.Series(0, index=time_index)
            try:
                arr_series = counts_time[(entity, "arrivals")]
            except KeyError:
                arr_series = pd.Series(0, index=time_index)

            any_event = (dep_series.fillna(0) + arr_series.fillna(0)) > 0
            hours_covered = int(any_event.sum())
            total_events = int(dep_series.sum()) + int(arr_series.sum())
            coverage.append(
                {
                    entity_type: entity,
                    "hours_covered": hours_covered,
                    "total_hours": total_buckets,
                    "hours_covered_ratio": (
                        hours_covered / total_buckets if total_buckets else 0.0
                    ),
                    "total_events": total_events,
                }
            )
        else:
            coverage.append(
                {
                    entity_type: entity,
                    "hours_covered": 0,
                    "total_hours": total_buckets,
                    "hours_covered_ratio": 0.0,
                    "total_events": 0,
                }
            )

    coverage_df = pd.DataFrame(coverage).set_index(entity_type)
    coverage_df["sufficient_coverage"] = (
        coverage_df["hours_covered"] >= min_hours_covered
    )

    return counts_time, counts_day, coverage_df

docs.title: create_concurrency_lookup_dataset
docs.text:
create_concurrency_lookup_dataset(df_flights: DataFrame, df_airports: Optional[DataFrame] = None, data_dir: Optional[Path] = None, output_filename: str = 'concurrency_lookup.csv', freq: str = 'H', by_groups: bool = True) -> Path

Create and save a concurrency lookup dataset for fast feature engineering.

This creates a flattened lookup table with columns: - datetime: hour timestamp - airport: airport code - airport_group: airport group (if available) - dep_concurrency: departures count for this hour - arr_concurrency: arrivals count for this hour - dep_concurrency_group: group departures (if by_groups=True) - arr_concurrency_group: group arrivals (if by_groups=True)

Returns the path to the saved dataset.

Source code in src/concurrency.py 
def create_concurrency_lookup_dataset(
    df_flights: pd.DataFrame,
    df_airports: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    data_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
    output_filename: str = "concurrency_lookup.csv",
    freq: str = "H",
    by_groups: bool = True,
) -> Path:
    """Create and save a concurrency lookup dataset for fast feature engineering.

    This creates a flattened lookup table with columns:
    - datetime: hour timestamp
    - airport: airport code
    - airport_group: airport group (if available)
    - dep_concurrency: departures count for this hour
    - arr_concurrency: arrivals count for this hour
    - dep_concurrency_group: group departures (if by_groups=True)
    - arr_concurrency_group: group arrivals (if by_groups=True)

    Returns the path to the saved dataset.
    """
    data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else DATA_DIR
    output_path = data_dir / output_filename

    print(f"Computing concurrency lookup dataset...")

    # Compute concurrency with groups
    counts_time, _, coverage_df = compute_concurrency_with_coverage(
        df_flights=df_flights,
        df_airports=df_airports,
        freq=freq,
        by_groups=by_groups,
        include_master_only=True,
    )

    # Create flattened lookup table
    lookup_records = []

    # Get time index
    time_index = counts_time.index

    # Process each timestamp
    for timestamp in time_index:
        timestamp_data = counts_time.loc[timestamp]

        # Extract departures and arrivals for each entity
        entities = timestamp_data.index.get_level_values(0).unique()

        for entity in entities:
            try:
                dep_count = timestamp_data.get((entity, "departures"), 0)
                arr_count = timestamp_data.get((entity, "arrivals"), 0)

                record = {
                    "datetime": timestamp,
                    "entity": entity,
                    "dep_concurrency": int(dep_count) if pd.notna(dep_count) else 0,
                    "arr_concurrency": int(arr_count) if pd.notna(arr_count) else 0,
                }

                lookup_records.append(record)

            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Warning: Error processing {entity} at {timestamp}: {e}")
                continue

    # Create DataFrame
    lookup_df = pd.DataFrame(lookup_records)

    if lookup_df.empty:
        print("Warning: No concurrency data generated")
        return output_path

    # Add airport group mapping if available
    # Try to load airport groups from separate file
    airport_group_map = {}
    if data_dir:
        airport_groups_file = data_dir / "avinor_data/airportgroups.csv"
        if airport_groups_file.exists():
            try:
                df_groups = pd.read_csv(airport_groups_file)
                if (
                    "airport" in df_groups.columns
                    and "airport_group" in df_groups.columns
                ):
                    airport_group_map = df_groups.set_index("airport")[
                        "airport_group"
                    ].to_dict()
                    print(f"   Loaded {len(airport_group_map)} airport group mappings")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"   Warning: Could not load airport groups: {e}")

    # Determine if entity is airport or group and add appropriate columns
    if by_groups:
        lookup_df["airport_group"] = lookup_df["entity"]
        lookup_df["airport"] = None  # Groups don't map to individual airports
    else:
        lookup_df["airport"] = lookup_df["entity"]
        lookup_df["airport_group"] = lookup_df["airport"].map(airport_group_map)
        # Fill NaN airport groups with the airport code itself as fallback
        lookup_df["airport_group"] = lookup_df["airport_group"].fillna(
            lookup_df["airport"]
        )

    # Sort and clean
    lookup_df = lookup_df.sort_values(["datetime", "entity"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Save dataset
    lookup_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

    print(f"Concurrency lookup dataset saved: {output_path}")
    print(f"   Shape: {lookup_df.shape}")
    print(
        f"   Time range: {lookup_df['datetime'].min()} to {lookup_df['datetime'].max()}"
    )
    print(f"   Entities: {lookup_df['entity'].nunique()}")

    return output_path

def load_concurrency_lookup(
    data_dir: Optional[Path] = None, filename: str = "concurrency_lookup.csv"

    """Load pre-computed concurrency lookup dataset.

    Returns None if file doesn't exist.

    lookup_path = data_dir / filename

        return None

Adds columns: - origin_departures_hour, origin_arrivals_hour (concurrency at departure airport) - dest_departures_hour, dest_arrivals_hour (concurrency at destination airport) - origin_group_departures_hour, origin_group_arrivals_hour (by airport group if available) - dest_group_departures_hour, dest_group_arrivals_hour

def add_concurrency_features(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    df_flights: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    df_airports: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    time_col: str = "flight_datetime_hour",
    origin_col: str = "dep_airport",
    dest_col: str = "arr_airport",
    data_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add concurrency features using cached lookup dataset for speed.

    First tries to load pre-computed concurrency data. If not found,
    falls back to computing on-the-fly.

    Adds columns:
    - origin_departures_hour, origin_arrivals_hour (concurrency at departure airport)
    - dest_departures_hour, dest_arrivals_hour (concurrency at destination airport)
    - origin_group_departures_hour, origin_group_arrivals_hour (by airport group if available)
    - dest_group_departures_hour, dest_group_arrivals_hour
    """
    from src.concurrency import (
        load_concurrency_lookup,
        create_concurrency_lookup_dataset,
    )

    if df is None or df.empty:
        return df

    out = df.copy()

    # Ensure time column exists and is datetime
    if time_col not in out.columns:
        return out

    out[time_col] = pd.to_datetime(out[time_col], utc=True).dt.floor("h")
    data_dir = data_dir or DATA_DIR

    # Try to load cached concurrency lookup
    concurrency_df = load_concurrency_lookup(data_dir)

    if concurrency_df is None:
        print("⚠️ No cached concurrency data found. Computing on-the-fly...")
        if df_flights is None:
            print(
                "⚠️ Cannot compute concurrency: no flight data provided. Skipping concurrency features."
            )
            return out

        # Fallback: create dataset on-the-fly
        try:
            create_concurrency_lookup_dataset(
                df_flights, df_airports, data_dir=data_dir, by_groups=True
            )
            concurrency_df = load_concurrency_lookup(data_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️ Failed to compute concurrency: {e}")
            return out

    if concurrency_df is None or concurrency_df.empty:
        print("⚠️ No concurrency data available. Skipping concurrency features.")
        return out

    # Prepare lookup data
    concurrency_df["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(
        concurrency_df["datetime"], utc=True
    ).dt.floor("h")

    # Determine if we have airport-level or group-level data
    has_airport_data = (
        "airport" in concurrency_df.columns and concurrency_df["airport"].notna().any()
    )
    has_group_data = (
        "airport_group" in concurrency_df.columns
        and concurrency_df["airport_group"].notna().any()
    )

    # Add airport-level concurrency features
    if has_airport_data:
        airport_lookup = concurrency_df[concurrency_df["airport"].notna()].copy()

        # Create efficient lookup dictionaries
        dep_lookup = airport_lookup.set_index(["datetime", "airport"])[
            "dep_concurrency"
        ].to_dict()
        arr_lookup = airport_lookup.set_index(["datetime", "airport"])[
            "arr_concurrency"
        ].to_dict()

        # Add origin airport concurrency
        if origin_col in out.columns:
            out["origin_departures_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    dep_lookup.get((row[time_col], row[origin_col]), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col)) and pd.notna(row.get(origin_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )
            out["origin_arrivals_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    arr_lookup.get((row[time_col], row[origin_col]), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col)) and pd.notna(row.get(origin_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )

        # Add destination airport concurrency
        if dest_col in out.columns:
            out["dest_departures_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    dep_lookup.get((row[time_col], row.get(dest_col)), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col)) and pd.notna(row.get(dest_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )
            out["dest_arrivals_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    arr_lookup.get((row[time_col], row.get(dest_col)), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col)) and pd.notna(row.get(dest_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )

    # Add group-level concurrency features
    if has_group_data:
        group_lookup = concurrency_df[concurrency_df["airport_group"].notna()].copy()

        # Create efficient lookup dictionaries for groups
        group_dep_lookup = group_lookup.set_index(["datetime", "airport_group"])[
            "dep_concurrency"
        ].to_dict()
        group_arr_lookup = group_lookup.set_index(["datetime", "airport_group"])[
            "arr_concurrency"
        ].to_dict()

        # Add origin group concurrency
        origin_group_col = "dep_airport_group"
        if origin_group_col in out.columns:
            out["origin_group_departures_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    group_dep_lookup.get((row[time_col], row.get(origin_group_col)), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col))
                    and pd.notna(row.get(origin_group_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )
            out["origin_group_arrivals_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    group_arr_lookup.get((row[time_col], row.get(origin_group_col)), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col))
                    and pd.notna(row.get(origin_group_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )

        # Add destination group concurrency
        dest_group_col = "arr_airport_group"
        if dest_group_col in out.columns:
            out["dest_group_departures_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    group_dep_lookup.get((row[time_col], row.get(dest_group_col)), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col)) and pd.notna(row.get(dest_group_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )
            out["dest_group_arrivals_hour"] = out.apply(
                lambda row: (
                    group_arr_lookup.get((row[time_col], row.get(dest_group_col)), 0)
                    if pd.notna(row.get(time_col)) and pd.notna(row.get(dest_group_col))
                    else 0
                ),
                axis=1,
            )

    # Fill any remaining NaN values with 0
    concurrency_cols = [
        col
        for col in out.columns
        if "concurrency" in col or "departures_hour" in col or "arrivals_hour" in col
    ]
    for col in concurrency_cols:
        out[col] = out[col].fillna(0)

    return out

Add temporal features and cyclical encodings based on time_col.

  • Keeps the original datetime column (does not drop it) so concatenation/joins remain simple.
  • Adds: hour, dayofweek, month, dayofyear, is_weekend
  • Adds cyclical encodings: hour_sin, hour_cos, dow_sin, dow_cos, month_sin, month_cos, doy_sin, doy_cos

Parameters - df: DataFrame to operate on (a copy is returned) - time_col: column name with datetimes; if missing, function will try 'datetime' - keep_datetime: if True (default) the datetime column remains; function never removes other columns.

Source code in src/feature_engineering.py 
def add_temporal_cyclical_features(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    time_col: str = "flight_datetime_hour",
    keep_datetime: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add temporal features and cyclical encodings based on `time_col`.

    - Keeps the original datetime column (does not drop it) so concatenation/joins
      remain simple.
    - Adds: hour, dayofweek, month, dayofyear, is_weekend
    - Adds cyclical encodings: hour_sin, hour_cos, dow_sin, dow_cos, month_sin, month_cos, doy_sin, doy_cos

    Parameters
    - df: DataFrame to operate on (a copy is returned)
    - time_col: column name with datetimes; if missing, function will try 'datetime'
    - keep_datetime: if True (default) the datetime column remains; function never removes other columns.
    """
    if df is None or df.empty:
        return df

    out = df.copy()

    col = (
        time_col
        if time_col in out.columns
        else ("datetime" if "datetime" in out.columns else None)
    )
    if col is None:
        # nothing to do
        return out

    out[col] = pd.to_datetime(out[col], utc=True)
    out[col] = out[col].dt.floor("h")

    out["hour"] = out[col].dt.hour
    out["dayofweek"] = out[col].dt.dayofweek
    out["month"] = out[col].dt.month
    out["dayofyear"] = out[col].dt.dayofyear
    out["is_weekend"] = out["dayofweek"].isin([5, 6]).astype(int)

    # cyclical encodings
    out["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * out["hour"] / 24)
    out["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * out["hour"] / 24)
    out["dow_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * out["dayofweek"] / 7)
    out["dow_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * out["dayofweek"] / 7)

    out["month_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (out["month"] - 1) / 12)
    out["month_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * (out["month"] - 1) / 12)

    out["doy_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (out["dayofyear"] - 1) / 365.25)
    out["doy_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * (out["dayofyear"] - 1) / 365.25)

    return out

def build_flight_weather_features(
    df_flights: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    df_weather: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    df_airports: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    data_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
    save: bool = False,
    out_filename: str = "flight_weather_features.csv",
    add_time_features: bool = True,
    compute_relative_wind: bool = True,
    include_concurrency_features: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Produce merged flight+weather features.

    If DataFrames are not provided the function will attempt to load them from
    disk under `data_dir` (default: project `data/` folder).

    Returns the merged DataFrame and optionally writes it to
    `data_dir/out_filename`.
    """
    # Delegate to the pipeline which returns the computed artifacts.
    pipeline_outputs = flight_weather_pipeline(
        df_flights=df_flights,
        df_weather=df_weather,
        df_airports=df_airports,
        data_dir=data_dir,
        add_time_features=add_time_features,
        compute_relative_wind=compute_relative_wind,
        include_concurrency_features=include_concurrency_features,
    )

    merged = pipeline_outputs["merged"]

    if save:
        save_flight_weather_features(
            merged, data_dir=data_dir, out_filename=out_filename
        )

    return merged

Compute flight-relative headwind and crosswind.

  • Attempts to find origin/destination airport columns among common names
  • Uses df_airports (expects iata_code, latitude, longitude) to get coords
  • Adds columns: flight_bearing_deg, wind_headwind, wind_crosswind

def compute_flight_relative_wind(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    df_airports: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    origin_col_candidates=None,
    dest_col_candidates=None,
    wind_speed_col: str = "wind_speed",
    wind_dir_col: str = "wind_direction",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute flight-relative headwind and crosswind.

    - Attempts to find origin/destination airport columns among common names
    - Uses `df_airports` (expects `iata_code`, `latitude`, `longitude`) to get coords
    - Adds columns: `flight_bearing_deg`, `wind_headwind`, `wind_crosswind`
    """
    if df is None or df.empty:
        return df

    out = df.copy()

    origin_candidates = origin_col_candidates or [
        "origin",
        "dep_airport",
        "departure_airport",
        "dep",
    ]
    dest_candidates = dest_col_candidates or [
        "destination",
        "arr_airport",
        "arrival_airport",
        "arr",
    ]

    origin_col = next((c for c in origin_candidates if c in out.columns), None)
    dest_col = next((c for c in dest_candidates if c in out.columns), None)

    # Helper: bearing calculation
    import math

    def _bearing(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
        try:
            lat1 = math.radians(lat1)
            lat2 = math.radians(lat2)
            diff_long = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
            x = math.sin(diff_long) * math.cos(lat2)
            y = math.cos(lat1) * math.sin(lat2) - (
                math.sin(lat1) * math.cos(lat2) * math.cos(diff_long)
            )
            initial_bearing = math.degrees(math.atan2(x, y))
            return (initial_bearing + 360) % 360
        except Exception:
            return np.nan

    # If coords already present in dataframe, use them
    if {"origin_lat", "origin_lon", "dest_lat", "dest_lon"}.issubset(out.columns):
        out["flight_bearing_deg"] = out.apply(
            lambda r: (
                _bearing(r["origin_lat"], r["origin_lon"], r["dest_lat"], r["dest_lon"])
                if pd.notna(r["origin_lat"]) and pd.notna(r["dest_lat"])
                else np.nan
            ),
            axis=1,
        )
    elif df_airports is not None and origin_col and dest_col:
        # build lookup
        coords = df_airports.set_index("iata_code")[["latitude", "longitude"]].to_dict(
            "index"
        )

        def lookup_coords(code):
            if pd.isna(code):
                return (np.nan, np.nan)
            if code in coords:
                return (coords[code]["latitude"], coords[code]["longitude"])
            return (np.nan, np.nan)

        out[["origin_lat", "origin_lon"]] = out[origin_col].apply(
            lambda c: pd.Series(lookup_coords(c))
        )
        out[["dest_lat", "dest_lon"]] = out[dest_col].apply(
            lambda c: pd.Series(lookup_coords(c))
        )

        out["flight_bearing_deg"] = out.apply(
            lambda r: (
                _bearing(r["origin_lat"], r["origin_lon"], r["dest_lat"], r["dest_lon"])
                if pd.notna(r["origin_lat"]) and pd.notna(r["dest_lat"])
                else np.nan
            ),
            axis=1,
        )
    else:
        # cannot compute bearing
        out["flight_bearing_deg"] = np.nan

    # Project wind onto flight bearing
    def project_head_cross(ws, wd, bearing):
        try:
            if pd.isna(ws) or pd.isna(wd) or pd.isna(bearing):
                return (np.nan, np.nan)
            # theta = angle between wind vector (from direction wd) and flight track
            theta = math.radians((wd - bearing + 360) % 360)
            head = ws * math.cos(theta)
            cross = ws * math.sin(theta)
            return (head, cross)
        except Exception:
            return (np.nan, np.nan)

    # compute head and cross
    comp = out.apply(
        lambda r: project_head_cross(
            r.get(wind_speed_col), r.get(wind_dir_col), r.get("flight_bearing_deg")
        ),
        axis=1,
    )
    comp_df = pd.DataFrame(
        comp.tolist(), index=out.index, columns=["wind_headwind", "wind_crosswind"]
    )
    out = pd.concat([out, comp_df], axis=1)

    return out

def flight_weather_pipeline(
    df_flights: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    df_weather: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    df_airports: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    data_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
    add_time_features: bool = True,
    compute_relative_wind: bool = True,
    include_concurrency_features: bool = True,
) -> dict:
    """Run a deterministic pipeline that returns intermediate artifacts.

    Returns a dict with keys: 'processed_flights', 'cleaned_weather', 'weather_features', 'merged'.
    The function does NOT save to disk — use `save_flight_weather_features` to persist.
    """
    dp = DataPreprocessor()
    data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir is not None else DATA_DIR

    # Load inputs if not provided
    if df_flights is None:
        flights_file = data_dir / "avinor_data/historical_flights.csv"
        if not flights_file.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Flights file not found: {flights_file}")
        df_flights = pd.read_csv(flights_file)

    if df_weather is None:
        w_complete = data_dir / "weather_data_complete.csv"
        w_main = data_dir / "weather_data.csv"
        weather_file = w_complete if w_complete.exists() else w_main
        if not weather_file.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"Weather file not found (tried {w_complete} and {w_main})"
            )
        df_weather = pd.read_csv(weather_file)

    if df_airports is None:
        airports_file = data_dir / "airport_coordinates.csv"
        if airports_file.exists():
            df_airports = pd.read_csv(airports_file)
        else:
            df_airports = None

    # Process flights (use non-cancelled historical by default)
    processed_flights = dp.process_hist_flights(df_flights)

    # Clean and feature-engineer weather
    cleaned_weather = dp.process_weather(df_weather)
    weather_features = dp.feature_engineer_weather(cleaned_weather)

    # Merge weather onto flights
    merged = dp.merge_weather_with_flights(
        weather_features, processed_flights, df_airports=df_airports
    )

    # Add temporal cyclical features to the merged flight rows (optional)
    if add_time_features:
        merged = add_temporal_cyclical_features(merged, time_col="flight_datetime_hour")

    # Compute flight-relative headwind and crosswind (optional)
    if compute_relative_wind:
        merged = compute_flight_relative_wind(merged, df_airports=df_airports)

    # Add concurrency features (optional)
    if include_concurrency_features:
        merged = add_concurrency_features(
            merged, df_flights=processed_flights, df_airports=df_airports
        )

    return {
        "processed_flights": processed_flights,
        "cleaned_weather": cleaned_weather,
        "weather_features": weather_features,
        "merged": merged,
    }

def feature_engineer_weather(self, df_weather: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    """Create useful features from cleaned hourly weather data.

    Adds:
    - temporal features: hour, dayofweek, month, is_weekend
    - cyclical transforms: hour_sin, hour_cos, dow_sin, dow_cos
    - short-term trends: temp_diff_1h, temp_roll_3h
    - wind vector components: wind_u, wind_v

    Input expects the dataframe returned from `process_weather` with columns
    including 'datetime' (datetime64[ns,UTC]) and 'wind_speed' & 'wind_direction'.
    """
    if df_weather is None or df_weather.empty:
        return df_weather.copy()

    df = df_weather.copy()

    if "datetime" not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("weather DataFrame must contain a `datetime` column")

    # Ensure datetime is timezone-aware and floored to the hour
    df["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(df["datetime"], utc=True).dt.floor("h")

    # Temporal features
    df["hour"] = df["datetime"].dt.hour
    df["dayofweek"] = df["datetime"].dt.dayofweek
    df["month"] = df["datetime"].dt.month
    df["is_weekend"] = df["dayofweek"].isin([5, 6]).astype(int)

    # Cyclical encodings
    df["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * df["hour"] / 24)
    df["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * df["hour"] / 24)
    df["dow_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * df["dayofweek"] / 7)
    df["dow_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * df["dayofweek"] / 7)

    # Short-term trends and rolling stats per airport (with NaN handling)
    df = df.sort_values(["airport", "datetime"])

    # Temperature difference (fill NaN with 0 = no change)
    df["temp_diff_1h"] = df.groupby("airport")["temperature"].diff().fillna(0.0)

    # Rolling temperature (always has min_periods=1, fill any remaining NaN)
    df["temp_roll_3h"] = (
        df.groupby("airport")["temperature"]
        .rolling(window=3, min_periods=1)
        .mean()
        .reset_index(level=0, drop=True)
    )
    df["temp_roll_3h"] = df["temp_roll_3h"].fillna(
        df["temperature"]
    )  # Fill with current temp if needed

    # Rolling precipitation (sum, fill NaN with 0)
    df["precip_roll_3h"] = (
        df.groupby("airport")["precipitation"]
        .rolling(window=3, min_periods=1)
        .sum()
        .reset_index(level=0, drop=True)
    )
    df["precip_roll_3h"] = df["precip_roll_3h"].fillna(0.0)

    # Wind vector components: convert degrees to radians; note convention: wind_direction is meteorological (degrees from north)
    # We compute u (east-west) and v (north-south) components where positive u = eastward, positive v = northward.
    if "wind_speed" in df.columns and "wind_direction" in df.columns:
        # meteorological wind_direction: degrees from north, clockwise. To convert to mathematical angle from east (for u/v):
        # theta_math = 90 - wind_dir
        theta = np.deg2rad(90 - df["wind_direction"].fillna(0))
        df["wind_u"] = df["wind_speed"].fillna(0) * np.cos(theta)
        df["wind_v"] = df["wind_speed"].fillna(0) * np.sin(theta)
    else:
        df["wind_u"] = np.nan
        df["wind_v"] = np.nan

    return df

  • If df_airports is provided and flight_dest_col exists, computes bearing from origin->destination and then headwind and crosswind components relative to that bearing.

def merge_weather_with_flights(
    self,
    df_weather: DataFrame,
    df_flights: DataFrame,
    df_airports: DataFrame = None,
    flight_time_col: str = "std",
    flight_origin_col: str = "origin",
    flight_dest_col: str = "destination",
) -> DataFrame:
    """Attach weather to flights and optionally compute headwind/crosswind components.

    - Merges weather onto flights by matching airport (origin) and floored hour of `flight_time_col`.
    - If `df_airports` is provided and `flight_dest_col` exists, computes bearing from origin->destination and
      then headwind and crosswind components relative to that bearing.

    NOTE: This function is permissive about column names but will raise informative errors if required columns
    are missing.
    """
    if df_flights is None or df_flights.empty:
        return df_flights.copy()

    flights = df_flights.copy()
    weather = df_weather.copy()

    # Ensure time columns
    if flight_time_col not in flights.columns:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Flights dataframe must contain time column `{flight_time_col}`"
        )

    # Floor times to hours for joining
    flights["flight_datetime_hour"] = pd.to_datetime(
        flights[flight_time_col], errors="coerce", utc=True
    ).dt.floor("h")
    weather["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(weather["datetime"], utc=True).dt.floor(
        "h"
    )

    # Determine origin column name
    if flight_origin_col not in flights.columns:
        # Try common alternatives
        alt = None
        for candidate in [
            "origin",
            "origin_airport",
            "dep_airport",
            "departure_airport",
            "airport",
        ]:
            if candidate in flights.columns:
                alt = candidate
                break
        if alt is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Could not find an origin airport column in flights dataframe"
            )
        flight_origin_col = alt

    # Merge weather (left join)
    merged = pd.merge(
        flights,
        weather,
        left_on=[flight_origin_col, "flight_datetime_hour"],
        right_on=["airport", "datetime"],
        how="left",
        suffixes=("", "_weather"),
    )

    # If airport coordinates and destination are available, compute bearing and wind components relative to flight
    if df_airports is not None and flight_dest_col in merged.columns:
        # Build coords lookup
        coords = df_airports.set_index("iata_code")[
            ["latitude", "longitude"]
        ].to_dict("index")

        def get_coords(code):
            if pd.isna(code):
                return (np.nan, np.nan)
            if code in coords:
                return (coords[code]["latitude"], coords[code]["longitude"])
            return (np.nan, np.nan)

        # origin coords
        merged[["origin_lat", "origin_lon"]] = merged[flight_origin_col].apply(
            lambda c: pd.Series(get_coords(c))
        )
        merged[["dest_lat", "dest_lon"]] = merged[flight_dest_col].apply(
            lambda c: pd.Series(get_coords(c))
        )

        # compute bearing origin->dest
        merged["flight_bearing_deg"] = merged.apply(
            lambda r: (
                self._calculate_bearing(
                    r["origin_lat"], r["origin_lon"], r["dest_lat"], r["dest_lon"]
                )
                if pd.notna(r["origin_lat"]) and pd.notna(r["dest_lat"])
                else np.nan
            ),
            axis=1,
        )

        # compute headwind & crosswind if wind available
        if "wind_speed" in merged.columns and "wind_direction" in merged.columns:
            # difference between wind direction (meteo) and flight bearing
            # wind_dir and flight_bearing are degrees; convert to radians
            def comp_head_cross(ws, wd, bearing):
                if pd.isna(ws) or pd.isna(wd) or pd.isna(bearing):
                    return (np.nan, np.nan)
                # relative angle: positive when wind is from ahead (headwind positive)
                # compute angle difference: wind comes from wd degrees (from north clockwise)
                # headwind = ws * cos(theta) where theta = angle between wind vector and aircraft ground-track
                theta = math.radians((wd - bearing + 360) % 360)
                head = ws * math.cos(theta)
                cross = ws * math.sin(theta)
                return (head, cross)

            comp = merged.apply(
                lambda r: comp_head_cross(
                    r["wind_speed"], r["wind_direction"], r["flight_bearing_deg"]
                ),
                axis=1,
            )
            comp_df = pd.DataFrame(
                comp.tolist(),
                index=merged.index,
                columns=["wind_headwind", "wind_crosswind"],
            )
            merged = pd.concat([merged, comp_df], axis=1)

    return merged

def process_hist_flights(self, df_hist: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    """General processing of historical flight data"""
    df_processed_hist = df_hist.copy()

    # Fill missing airport groups with "OUT"
    df_processed_hist["arr_airport_group"] = df_processed_hist[
        "arr_airport_group"
    ].fillna("OUT")
    df_processed_hist["dep_airport_group"] = df_processed_hist[
        "dep_airport_group"
    ].fillna("OUT")

    # Fill missing service_type values within each flight_id group and keep original format
    df_processed_hist["service_type"] = df_processed_hist["service_type"].fillna(
        "X"
    )

    # Drop rows where cancelled is 1
    df_processed_hist = df_processed_hist[df_processed_hist["cancelled"] == 0]

    std_parsed = (
        pd.to_datetime(df_processed_hist["std"])
        if "std" in df_processed_hist.columns
        else None
    )
    sta_parsed = (
        pd.to_datetime(df_processed_hist["sta"])
        if "sta" in df_processed_hist.columns
        else None
    )

    df_processed_hist["std"] = std_parsed
    df_processed_hist["sta"] = sta_parsed

    atd_parsed = (
        pd.to_datetime(df_processed_hist["atd"])
        if "atd" in df_processed_hist.columns
        else None
    )
    ata_parsed = (
        pd.to_datetime(df_processed_hist["ata"])
        if "ata" in df_processed_hist.columns
        else None
    )

    df_processed_hist["atd"] = atd_parsed
    df_processed_hist["ata"] = ata_parsed

    # remove cancelled column
    df_processed_hist = df_processed_hist.drop(columns=["cancelled"])
    print("Missing values after processing:")
    print(df_processed_hist.isna().sum())

    print("dropping rows with missing actual times")
    df_processed_hist = df_processed_hist.dropna(subset=["atd", "ata"])
    print("Final missing values:")
    print(df_processed_hist.isna().sum())
    return df_processed_hist

def process_hist_flights_cancelled(self, df_hist: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    """General processing of historical flight data and removal of unused columns"""
    # Historical Flights
    # todo: missing atd and ata:
    # train a model without these values, predict these values, and train a model with these values
    # or completely drop these rows

    df_processed_hist = df_hist.copy()

    std_parsed = (
        pd.to_datetime(df_processed_hist["std"])
        if "std" in df_processed_hist.columns
        else None
    )
    sta_parsed = (
        pd.to_datetime(df_processed_hist["sta"])
        if "sta" in df_processed_hist.columns
        else None
    )

    df_processed_hist["std"] = std_parsed
    df_processed_hist["sta"] = sta_parsed

    # Sort by std (scheduled time of departure)
    df_processed_hist = df_processed_hist.sort_values("std")

    # set cancelled to 1 if atd and ata are missing
    df_processed_hist[
        df_processed_hist["cancelled"].isna()
        | df_processed_hist["ata"].isna() & df_processed_hist["atd"].isna()
    ]["cancelled"] = 1

    # drop actual times for cancellation prediction
    df_processed_hist = df_processed_hist.drop(columns=["atd", "ata"])

    # Fill missing
    df_processed_hist["arrival_airport_group"] = df_processed_hist[
        "arrival_airport_group"
    ].fillna("OUT")
    df_processed_hist["departure_airport_group"] = df_processed_hist[
        "departure_airport_group"
    ].fillna("OUT")

    print("Missing values after processing:")
    print(df_processed_hist.isna().sum())

    return df_processed_hist

def process_weather(self, df_weather: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    """Clean and standardize raw weather dataframe.

    - Normalize common column names (temperature_2m -> temperature, etc.)
    - Parse timestamps to UTC and floor to the hour
    - Keep a sensible set of columns
    - Drop duplicates and sort
    - Interpolate small gaps (per-airport)

    Returns a cleaned DataFrame with at least columns:
    ['airport', 'datetime', 'temperature', 'humidity', 'precipitation',
     'pressure', 'cloud_cover', 'wind_speed', 'wind_direction', 'visibility',
     'latitude', 'longitude'] (columns may be absent if not in source)
    """
    if df_weather is None or df_weather.empty:
        return df_weather.copy()

    df = df_weather.copy()

    # Common renames from Open-Meteo and other sources
    rename_map = {
        "time": "datetime",
        "temperature_2m": "temperature",
        "relative_humidity_2m": "humidity",
        "precipitation": "precipitation",
        "surface_pressure": "pressure",
        "cloud_cover": "cloud_cover",
        "wind_speed_10m": "wind_speed",
        "wind_direction_10m": "wind_direction",
        "visibility": "visibility",
        "airport_code": "airport",
        "iata_code": "airport",
    }

    df = df.rename(columns={k: v for k, v in rename_map.items() if k in df.columns})

    # Ensure datetime is parsed
    if "datetime" in df.columns:
        df["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(df["datetime"], errors="coerce", utc=True)
        # also add a floored hour column for easy joins
        df["datetime"] = df["datetime"].dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    else:
        # try to infer from common names
        raise ValueError(
            "Input weather DataFrame must contain a datetime/time column"
        )

    # Floor to the hour (we treat hourly weather)
    df["datetime"] = df["datetime"].dt.floor("h")

    # Standard column set we keep if present
    keep_cols = [
        "airport",
        "datetime",
        "temperature",
        "humidity",
        "precipitation",
        "pressure",
        "cloud_cover",
        "wind_speed",
        "wind_direction",
        "visibility",
        "latitude",
        "longitude",
    ]

    existing_keep = [c for c in keep_cols if c in df.columns]
    df = df[existing_keep].copy()

    # Drop exact duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates()

    # Sort and reset index
    df = df.sort_values(["airport", "datetime"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Apply intelligent weather trend-based NaN filling
    df = self._fill_weather_gaps_with_trends(df)

    return df
